defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The ST sample exhibits the highest KAM intensity and the steepest gradients at grain boundaries, indicative of severe strain localization and impeded slip transmission with dislocation pile-ups during cyclic loading.

interfaces.interface_notes: Grain boundaries in ST show the highest KAM intensity and steepest gradients, indicating severe strain localization and impeded slip transmission with dislocation pile-ups.
interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar dislocation slip occurs via the 'glide plane softening' effect from short-range ordering (SRO); SRO-driven softening is weak and spatially heterogeneous, promoting cross-slip and local strain concentration, giving low slip reversibility in ST. Under fatigue, ST shows local wavy slip (cross slip) at Δσ/2 = 180 MPa and kink bands at Δσ/2 = 315 MPa.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: fatigue strength (maximum stress amplitude sustained for 10^7 cycles without failure) and fatigue life

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 50 kg ingot was prepared by vacuum melting.
forged into a billet with a cross-section of 30 mm × 30 mm
hot-rolled to a final thickness of 4 mm
Solution treatment at 1050 °C for 1 h, followed by water quenching to room temperature; this condition is referred to as ST (fully austenitic reference condition without aging-induced κ-carbides).

structures.overall_structure: Fully austenitic microstructure; fully equiaxed, single-phase austenitic grain structure with no second phase visible.

unmapped_findings: ST sample tested at Δσ/2 = 180 MPa shows crack-initiation-plus-propagation zone area fraction fΔ = 0.53; at Δσ/2 = 315 MPa, fΔ = 0.25, the smallest among ST/aged samples, consistent with its shorter fatigue life (b0041, figure_006).
ST rapid fracture zones are predominantly characterized by dimples, indicating a microvoid coalescence mechanism and ductile failure at both Δσ/2 = 180 MPa and 315 MPa (b0043, figure_008).

In the ST sample, fatigue striations in the crack propagation zone are relatively sparse/widely spaced at 180 MPa and wavy, widely spaced at 315 MPa, indicating a higher crack propagation rate than in 550-6 and 600-6 (b0042, figure_007).
In the ST sample, the fatigue crack path within large austenite grains is relatively straight, whereas aged samples show greater path tortuosity and microbranching (b0045, figure_009).
ST lacks intragranular κ-carbides and therefore exhibits the lowest fatigue strength (157.5 MPa at 10^7 cycles) among ST, 550-6 (162 MPa), 600-6 (175.5 MPa) and 650-6 (171 MPa) (b0035, b0066).
